name: switchblade
concept: A protocol-agnostic service knife that fingerpoints host/port/service combos across SSH, FTP, SMTP, HTTP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, mDNS and SMB, carries a lightweight library of service-specific misconfig/weak-cred check operators, and runs an autonomous triage/orchestration brain that scores each discovered path by exploit-likelihood and drops the highest-confidence attack against allowlisted lab hosts only.
attack_vectors: service banner/fingerprint match vs known-misconfig signature table
default/weak credential login attempts per protocol (SSH, FTP, MySQL, Postgres, Redis, SMB)
unauthenticated Redis/Postgres/HTTP endpoints (no-auth keyspace, exposed admin pages)
mDNS/SMB enum for shares + weak guest/anonymous access on lab hosts
version-driven CVE signature match to launch a canned exploit check
novelty_angle: Most lab knives scan fast and stop at fingerprints; this one adds a self-adapting triage brain that re-scans candidate services at higher depth, learns which check types scored hits in-session, biases the queue toward the best-evidence path, and emits ranked exploit candidates — a scan tool that reasons about what to hit next rather than blind scripted checks.
dependencies: json for scope allowlist + state persistence
banner-parsing regex lib for fingerprint signatures
scope_gate: Loads an allowlist (loopback 127.0.0.0/8, RFC1918 private ranges, plus user-supplied lab CIDR) into a set; every target IP is checked against this set before connect/probe/exploit; any address outside triggers immediate abort for that target + red WARN banner before any network activity.
